tagline: Seven thousand feet in 28 miles, and 25 feet to spare.
intro: From Idaho Springs, the 1859 gold camp in Clear Creek Canyon, Highway 103 climbs thirteen miles to Echo Lake. There Highway 5 takes over for fifteen miles more, through a corridor left out of the wilderness, to a turnaround just below the summit of Mount Blue Sky. In 28 miles the road gains more than 7,000 feet and climbs above timberline. It is the highest paved road in North America, ahead of the Pikes Peak Highway by 25 feet.

Denver's mountain parks system planned it to link Echo Lake and Summit Lake to its foothill parks, on a route set by Frederick Law Olmsted Jr. The mountain was Mount Evans until 2023, when it was renamed Mount Blue Sky.

moments.title: Echo Lake
moments.text: A lake at 10,600 feet held back by glacial moraines, with a 1926 octagonal log lodge on a base of local granite that resembles a Native American earth lodge.

moments.title: Summit Lake
moments.text: A tarn at 12,836 feet in a cirque on the mountain's north face, with permafrost on its east side and some summer wildflowers found nowhere else outside the Arctic Circle.

moments.title: Mount Blue Sky
moments.text: Arthur Compton came up to study cosmic rays in 1931, shortly after the road reached the top, and carmakers test cars on the road, some in zebra-striped camouflage.

practical: The road from Echo Lake to the summit is open Memorial Day through Labor Day and requires a vehicle reservation. It is often narrow, with sudden drop-offs and no guardrails, and the state does not recommend it for vehicles over 30 feet long.
